alarms.name: Mold Protect Trip
alarms.whatTriggers: The mold hit resistance inside the low-pressure protect window and couldn't reach clamp-up within the allowed force/time. The machine stopped instead of crushing whatever is in there.
alarms.safeFirstResponse: STOP. Do not raise protect pressure to push through. Open the mold and physically inspect BOTH faces — look for a hung part, runner, cold slug, or a lifted insert/pin.
rootCauses: Part or runner left hanging after ejection (the #1 cause) — watch a full ejection with your own eyes; see Sticking
Cold slug or flash debris on a mold face
Protect window mis-set after a mold change — start position below the tallest possible hang-up, or pressure set too low for this tool's normal drag
Sprue picker / robot missed its grab
Mechanical: tight leader pins, low lube, platen parallelism
alarms.prevention: After every mold change, re-verify: protect start just above the tallest possible obstruction, lowest pressure that closes an empty mold reliably. Fix ejection reliability instead of numbing the protection.

alarms.name: Dose Not Complete
alarms.whatTriggers: The screw failed to reach the dose position within the allowed time — the next shot never got fully prepared.
alarms.safeFirstResponse: Check material supply first: hopper level, loader running, slide gate open. It's embarrassing how often this alarm means 'empty hopper.'
rootCauses: No/low material: hopper empty, loader fault, slide gate closed
Bridging in the feed throat — throat running warm; pellets sticking together above the screw
Back pressure too high or RPM too low for the required recovery
Worn screw/barrel or leaking check ring — screw spins but doesn't convey
Material issue: high regrind fines, oversize regrind, blended contaminant
alarms.prevention: Trend Dose Time — it stretches for hours before this alarm fires. Keep throat cooling verified on the startup checklist.

alarms.name: Minimum Cushion Alarm
alarms.whatTriggers: Min Cushion fell below its monitored limit — the screw is running out of melt before packing finished.
alarms.safeFirstResponse: Check the last parts for shorts/sinks, then look at the cushion trend: sudden drop or slow bleed?
rootCauses: Check ring leaking — the classic; cushion wanders then collapses (run Flow-Check / static leak test)
Shot size too small for the part + cushion (raise Dose Position)
V-P transfer moved later, eating the reserve
Melt got thinner (hotter/wetter) so more material packs in before the screw bottoms
New mold/cavity condition taking more material (e.g., vent/flash path opened)
alarms.prevention: Give yourself a real cushion (not fractions of a mm) and monitor it — cushion is the canary for check-ring health.

alarms.name: Fill Time / Pressure Limit Alarm
alarms.whatTriggers: Fill exceeded the Fill Time Limit, or injection pressure hit the Maximum Filling Pressure hard enough to stall progress — the shot couldn't get in.
alarms.safeFirstResponse: Don't just widen the limit. Check the obvious blockers: material in the barrel? Nozzle frozen? Gate blocked by a cold slug?
rootCauses: Nozzle freeze-off or cold slug blocking the tip (nozzle temp / suck back balance)
Empty barrel — see Dose Not Complete upstream
Genuine viscosity jump: cold melt, wrong material loaded, dryer down
Pressure limit set with no headroom — normal variation now clips it
Check ring failed — screw moves but melt goes backward
alarms.prevention: Keep 10-20% headroom between Fill Peak and the pressure limit; trend Fill Time so drift is caught before the alarm.

alarms.name: Heater Deviation / Thermocouple Fault
alarms.whatTriggers: A temperature zone drifted outside its allowed band, or its sensor reads open/erratic.
alarms.safeFirstResponse: Identify WHICH zone and WHICH direction. A zone stuck HIGH (possible stuck-on relay) is a runaway risk — get maintenance/supervision involved; don't just acknowledge and keep molding.
rootCauses: Thermocouple loose, damaged, or unplugged (reads low or erratic → zone overheats trying to chase it)
Heater band burned out or connector failed (zone can't reach setpoint)
Solid-state relay stuck ON (zone climbs past setpoint — the dangerous one) or stuck OFF
Band loose on the barrel — poor contact, slow lying readings
alarms.prevention: Degraded material and splay often show up before the alarm — a zone that 'takes forever to heat' is a heater on its way out.

alarms.name: Servo Torque Overload (Dose / Injection Axis)
alarms.whatTriggers: A servo axis (usually screw rotation) exceeded its torque limit — the all-electric equivalent of a hydraulic relief blowing.
alarms.safeFirstResponse: Do NOT keep retrying rotation. Verify every barrel zone is AT setpoint and has soaked 10-15+ minutes. Rotating a screw in half-melted plastic is how screws snap.
rootCauses: Cold start / insufficient heat soak (the classic — and the expensive one)
Foreign object in the feed (metal, oversize regrind) jamming the flights
Back pressure set excessively high for the material
Very stiff/filled resin with rear zones too cold
Mechanical: drive/bearing problem (persistent overloads at temp)
alarms.prevention: Enforce a soak timer after heats reach setpoint. Magnet in the feed path if regrind is in play.

alarms.name: Clamp Force Correction Fault
alarms.whatTriggers: The auto tonnage correction system can't reach or hold the set clamp force within its adjustment range.
alarms.safeFirstResponse: Check for anything physically between the platens and confirm the mold is seated/bolted correctly before re-homing anything.
rootCauses: Mold-height setup off after a mold change (correction runs out of travel)
Large thermal swing pushed the toggle outside the correction window
Tie-bar strain unbalanced — parallelism, uneven mold, or a bent issue (check CF1-CF4 spread)
Lubrication / mechanical drag in the toggle
Load-cell or sensor fault
alarms.prevention: Re-run mold height setup on every change; watch the CF1-CF4 per-tie-bar values for balance — big spread is a mechanical warning.

alarms.name: Safety Door / Purge Guard Interlock
alarms.whatTriggers: A guarded door or purge shield is open or its switch isn't satisfied — motion is locked out.
alarms.safeFirstResponse: It's doing its job. Close/verify the guard. NEVER bypass, jumper, or tape a safety switch — molten plastic and clamp motion are the two things on this machine that maim.
rootCauses: Door not fully closed / slammed out of alignment
Switch or actuator misaligned, worn, or damaged
Purge guard open from the last purge
Wiring/connector fault on the interlock circuit (maintenance)
alarms.prevention: Report sticky or misaligned guards immediately — a guard people fight with is a guard someone will eventually defeat.

alarms.name: Ejector Fault (Position / Return)
alarms.whatTriggers: The ejector plate didn't reach its commanded position or didn't confirm return before the mold was allowed to close.
alarms.safeFirstResponse: Inspect the mold: a jammed part or broken pin can be holding the plate. Confirm the plate is fully back before any close attempt.
rootCauses: Part jammed in the ejection path
Return confirmation (limit/proximity) switch misadjusted or failed
Ejector settings asking for travel the mold doesn't have (stroke past mechanical stop)
Broken/bent pin or return spring binding the plate
Speed/pressure too low to overcome release force (see Sticking)
alarms.prevention: After mold changes, verify ejector stroke against the tool's actual travel before running auto.

alarms.name: Nozzle Freeze-Off / Clog
alarms.whatTriggers: Melt can't get through the nozzle — fill stalls immediately, pressure spikes at zero progress, or purging produces nothing.
alarms.safeFirstResponse: Treat a blocked, heated nozzle as pressurized. Follow safe purge procedure — shields down, nobody in line with the nozzle, never look into or probe a hot nozzle from the front.
rootCauses: Nozzle temp too low or its heater failed — tip frozen against the cold sprue bushing
Excessive suck back pulled cold material into the tip which then froze
Foreign object or char lodged in the tip orifice
Long idle at temperature let the tip drain/set up
Wrong tip orifice vs sprue bushing (chronic version)
alarms.prevention: Balance nozzle temp with suck back rather than maxing either; on shutdowns, purge and back the carriage off the bushing.

alarms.name: Robot Waiting on Mold Open (No Descent)
alarms.whatTriggers: The robot is paused at the top of its stroke and never enters the mold. It hasn't received (or doesn't trust) the mold-fully-open signal from the press, so descent is not permitted.
alarms.safeFirstResponse: Don't reach in or jog the arm down manually. Check the press side first: did the mold actually reach its full-open position, or did it stop short? The robot refusing to descend is usually the press not finishing, not the robot failing.
rootCauses: Mold open stroke ends short of the position the robot was taught to expect — open position changed after a mold change
Mold-open limit / confirmation signal not reaching the robot (interface cable, relay, or signal assignment)
Robot descent-permit conditions not met — a previous cycle fault latched and needs a reset
Press stopped mid-open on its own alarm — clear the press alarm first
Robot in a mode that blocks auto descent (step mode, teach mode left active)
alarms.prevention: After any mold change or open-stroke adjustment, confirm the robot descent position was re-verified against the new open position before running auto.

alarms.name: Vacuum Confirmation Fault (Pickup Not Confirmed)
alarms.whatTriggers: The arm went in for the part, but the vacuum switch never confirmed a sealed grip within the allowed time — the robot doesn't believe it's holding the part.
alarms.safeFirstResponse: Stop and look in the mold before resuming: is the part still on the core, half-ejected, or already dropped loose in the mold area? A loose part in the mold plus an auto restart is how platens get smashed. Remove any loose part first.
rootCauses: Part not presented where the EOAT expects it — ejection short, slow, or part sticking (see Sticking)
Vacuum cup worn, split, or folded over — won't seal against the part surface
Vacuum switch threshold set too tight, or switch drifted — grip is real but never 'confirms'
Supply problem: low air pressure to the venturi, kinked or popped-off vacuum line
EOAT position drifted (loose mounting, crash earlier in the shift) so cups land off the part
alarms.prevention: Make cup condition and EOAT bolt check part of the mold-change checklist; keep a spare cup set at the press. Fix ejection consistency rather than adding retry attempts.

alarms.name: Chuck / Runner Grip Confirmation Fault
alarms.whatTriggers: A mechanical gripper (part chuck or runner grabber) closed but its confirmation sensor never made — the robot can't verify it actually caught anything.
alarms.safeFirstResponse: Same rule as a vacuum fault: inspect the mold area for a loose part or runner before any restart. Then cycle the gripper by hand (in manual, arm clear of the mold) and watch whether the confirm sensor light comes on.
rootCauses: Runner/part not in the expected position — sprue stuck in the bushing, runner hanging on a pin
Gripper closed on nothing (missed grab) because the taught position drifted
Confirm sensor (reed switch / proximity) loose, dead, or its cable damaged at a flex point
Low air pressure — gripper closes too slowly or without full force
Debris or flash packed into the gripper jaws
alarms.prevention: Check gripper sensors during weekly PM — wiggle the cables at the flex points; that's where they fail. Keep the sprue puller and runner geometry consistent so the grab point doesn't wander.

alarms.name: Part Lost During Transfer (Drop Detected)
alarms.whatTriggers: Vacuum or grip confirmation was lost mid-traverse — the robot picked the part, then dropped it somewhere between the mold and the release point.
alarms.safeFirstResponse: Find the part before restarting. If it's not on the floor or the conveyor, assume it's inside the machine or on the safety guarding — a part lodged on the tie bars or platen edge will cause a crash or mold damage next cycle.
rootCauses: Marginal grip from the start: worn cups, part gripped off-center, vacuum just above threshold
Traverse acceleration too aggressive for the part weight/grip — part peels off mid-move
Vacuum line rubbing/pinching at a flex point, losing vacuum only in certain arm positions
Part geometry or surface (texture, release spray) reducing seal quality
Air supply dip when other equipment on the same line cycles
alarms.prevention: Set vacuum confirm thresholds with margin above the drop point, and re-verify grip after any EOAT repair. If drops correlate with one arm position, inspect the vacuum line at that flex point.

alarms.name: Release Confirmation Fault (Part Didn't Drop)
alarms.whatTriggers: At the release position the robot opened the gripper / broke vacuum, but the part-present signal says the part is still on the EOAT.
alarms.safeFirstResponse: Go look at the EOAT. Usually the part is genuinely stuck to a cup or hung on the gripper. Remove it by hand with the robot in manual and motion stopped — not while it's trying to retry.
rootCauses: Part stuck to a vacuum cup (static, tacky material, release blow-off not working)
Blow-off air not plumbed/firing at release, so nothing pushes the part off
Part hung on gripper jaw or EOAT frame edge
Part-present sensor stuck or dirty — part actually released but sensor still reads 'present'
Release position over a full bin/conveyor backing parts up into the EOAT
alarms.prevention: Keep blow-off working and cups clean; check the part-present sensor face when this repeats. Watch for conveyor backups at the release station.

alarms.name: Arm Not Clear / Mold Area Interference
alarms.whatTriggers: The press is refusing to close (or the robot refuses to move) because the arm-clear signal says the robot is still inside the mold area. Press and robot are each waiting on the other.
alarms.safeFirstResponse: Never bypass or jumper the mold-area-free signal to get the press moving — that interlock is the only thing preventing the mold from closing on the arm. Verify visually where the arm actually is, then recover in manual.
rootCauses: Robot stopped mid-cycle (fault, e-stop) while physically inside the mold area — needs manual recovery to a safe position first
Arm-up / arm-clear confirmation sensor failed or misadjusted, so a genuinely clear arm never reports clear
Taught retract position doesn't fully satisfy the clear-zone sensor after a program edit
Interface signal issue between robot and press (cable, connector, relay)
Wrong program selected for this mold — arm path enters zones the press doesn't expect
alarms.prevention: After any program edit or crash, verify arm-clear confirmation triggers at the retract position before running auto. Treat any 'works if I jiggle it' interface cable as an immediate replacement.

alarms.name: Home / Origin Return Not Complete
alarms.whatTriggers: The robot doesn't know where its axes are — after a power cycle, e-stop, or crash it requires an origin (home) return before it will run, and that return didn't complete.
alarms.safeFirstResponse: Before commanding home, look at the whole travel path: homing moves axes to their reference ends, and if the arm is inside the mold or the EOAT is tangled with anything, homing will drag it. Clear the path, then home.
rootCauses: Arm physically obstructed along the homing path (inside mold, against guarding, cable snag)
Home/reference sensor dirty, loose, or dead — axis moves but never sees its reference
E-stop or safety circuit still open, blocking motion entirely
Axis brake not releasing (vertical axis) — common after long idle
Encoder/battery issue on absolute-encoder models: position memory lost and axis needs re-referencing per the manual
alarms.prevention: Power down the robot properly (not mid-motion), and address encoder battery warnings promptly instead of clearing them — they end as a no-home condition at the worst time.

alarms.name: Axis Overtravel / Limit Fault
alarms.whatTriggers: An axis ran past its allowed travel and hit a limit switch or software limit — the robot stopped to protect itself.
alarms.safeFirstResponse: Don't just reset and rerun the same program. An overtravel in auto means a taught position or offset is wrong, something slipped, or the robot was jogged there manually — find which before resuming.
rootCauses: Taught point edited beyond the axis range (or with the wrong sign) in a recent program change
Wrong program for the mold on the press — positions valid for a different setup
Mechanical slip: loose coupling or belt letting the actual position drift from the encoder's belief
Manually jogged into the limit during teaching or recovery
Limit switch itself loose or failing, tripping early
alarms.prevention: Verify edited positions by single-stepping the program at low speed before auto. Keep program names tied clearly to mold numbers so the wrong-program mistake is hard to make.

alarms.name: Servo Axis Alarm (Overload / Encoder)
alarms.whatTriggers: A servo drive tripped on overload, overcurrent, deviation (position error), or an encoder fault — the drive shut the axis down to protect the motor.
alarms.safeFirstResponse: One reset attempt is diagnostic; repeated resets are abuse. If it trips again, note the exact alarm number from the pendant — servo alarm codes are specific and the manual's code table will name the actual failure.
rootCauses: Mechanical binding raising the load: dry linear rails, damaged bearing, crash debris in the track
Overload from carrying more than the axis is rated for at the set speeds/accelerations
Deviation error: axis commanded but obstructed — it fell behind where it should be
Encoder cable damage at a flex point (intermittent position feedback)
Drive/motor genuinely failing — usually preceded by weeks of occasional trips
alarms.prevention: Keep rails lubed per the PM schedule and log every servo alarm with its code and axis — the pattern (same axis, same move) is what separates mechanical binding from electrical failure.

alarms.name: Low Air Pressure
alarms.whatTriggers: Supply air to the robot fell below its minimum. Everything pneumatic — vacuum venturis, grippers, blow-off, some brakes — becomes unreliable, so the robot stops rather than gamble.
alarms.safeFirstResponse: Check the robot's own regulator/gauge first, then work upstream: is it just this drop, this line, or the whole shop header? A part held only by marginal vacuum may drop when you restore motion — clear the area under the arm.
rootCauses: Shop air dip — compressor cycling, dryer down, or a big consumer starting up on the same header
Regulator on the robot drifted low or its filter bowl is clogged
Leak on the robot: popped fitting, cut line at a flex point (audible hiss)
Isolation valve partially closed after maintenance
Pressure switch itself drifted — pressure is fine but the switch reads low
alarms.prevention: Drain filter bowls and listen for new leaks during weekly PM. If the alarm coincides with another machine's cycle, the header is undersized or a line is restricted — fix the supply, don't lower the switch threshold.

alarms.name: Emergency Stop / Safety Circuit Open
alarms.whatTriggers: An e-stop or safety circuit in the robot/press cell opened — robot e-stop button, press e-stop, safety gate, or the interface between them. All motion is cut until the whole chain is closed and reset.
alarms.safeFirstResponse: Find out WHY it was hit before resetting — walk the cell. If you didn't press it and no one owns up, treat it as a real event (someone saw something), not a nuisance.
rootCauses: Someone pressed an e-stop — robot pendant, press panel, or cell button
Safety gate/door opened while in auto
E-stop chain between press and robot broken: interface cable, connector, safety relay
A button physically stuck/twisted in the latched position
Safety relay or door switch failing intermittently — the 'ghost' e-stop that needs tracing, not resetting
alarms.prevention: Label every e-stop in the cell and test each one on a schedule. Intermittent safety-circuit drops are a wiring fault to be traced with the print — never bridged.

alarms.name: Take-Out Not Complete / Press Waiting on Robot
alarms.whatTriggers: The robot didn't finish its take-out sequence within the allowed window, so the press is sitting open, waiting. Cycle time is bleeding away even if no hard fault shows.
alarms.safeFirstResponse: Watch one full cycle from a safe spot and find where the robot hesitates — waiting at descent, slow confirm at pickup, retries at release. The pause location tells you which fault above is brewing.
rootCauses: Marginal vacuum/grip confirmation taking multiple attempts before succeeding
Robot speed/acceleration turned down during earlier troubleshooting and never restored
Ejection presenting the part inconsistently — robot waits or retries (see Sticking)
Downstream backup: conveyor full, box change, degating station jammed — robot waits to release
Interlock signal slow or intermittent (mold-open confirm, ejector-permit handshake)
alarms.prevention: Know your normal robot-in-mold time and total cycle; trend it like Cycle Time. A creeping take-out time is an early warning you get for free.
